speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng
text: asked the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills) whether the Ministry will consider creating a SkillsFuture-equivalent scheme for Singaporeans aged under 25 to help them pursue extra-curricular training or enrichment courses which may not be available in their present educational institution.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Such programmes could either be conducted by the PSEIs or external organisers, but are approved by the PSEIs.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Examples include overseas attachments, leadership training courses, short study trips or tours, community involvement programmes, seminars, workshops and conferences.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: The PSEA thus supports our young Singaporeans in accessing learning opportunities over a wide spectrum of programmes.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Our young Singaporeans are empowered to take charge of their learning needs, so that they can be future-ready and economically relevant.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: Nonetheless, we note Dr Tan's suggestion that there may be other programmes that could be included under the coverage of PSEA.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: We acknowledge that the learning space is dynamic.

speaker: The Parliamentary Secretary to the Ministers for Education (Ms Low Yen Ling) (for the Minister for Education (Higher Education and Skills))
text: We want to assure Dr Tan that we review the coverage of PSEA regularly, with the intention of providing even more options for young Singaporeans.

speaker: Dr Tan Wu Meng (Jurong)
text: Would her Ministry be willing to comment on whether there is an increased role for having more skills ladders, more stacking of educational modules, with a view to helping these young folks transit seamlessly to adult education as they grow and mature?

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: So, indeed, we want to ensure that from the PSEA-supported courses, moving to the SkillsFuture Credit course directory, it is a bit more seamless.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Having said that, I would like to take the opportunity to reiterate that the SkillsFuture movement is really not just about SkillsFuture Credit.

speaker: Ms Low Yen Ling
text: Because the Member asked about Singaporeans younger than 25 years old, it gave us the opportunity to talk about the PSEA.
